saa-ini-302.text: Which ones DUAS statements correctly compare volumes Amazon EBS and Forum Store? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: The Forum Store persists data even after the instance is closed (final)
Volumes EBS may be desynched from one instance and attached to the other in the same AZ
The EBS does not allow creating snapshots
The Forum Store is local physical storage of the host, with data lost in case of stop or end of instance
Volumes EBS can only be created together with the instance and never later
saa-ini-302.explanation: A) Incorrect: the Forum Store is ephemeral — the data is lost on the stop/terminate. B) Correct: EBS it is persistent network storage and independent of the instance life cycle, and can be moved between instances of the same AZ. C) Incorrect: snapshots are a central resource of the EBS (incremental backups no S3). D) Correct: the Forum Store is the host's physical disk, with very high performance, but ephemeral. E) Incorrect: volumes EBS can be created and attached at any time.

saa-ini-303.text: Which ones DUAS statements on the AWS Lambda Are they correct? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: A performance of the function can last as long as possible 15 minutes
The Lambda requires the prior provisioning of instances EC2 to execute the code
The Lambda charges a monthly fixed value per function created, even without executions
Increasing the configured memory of a function also increases proportionally to CPU available
Functions Lambda cannot access resources within a VPC
saa-ini-303.explanation: A) Correct: the maximum timeout of an execution is 15 minutes — longer tasks ask Fargate, Batch or Step Functions. B) Incorrect: or Lambda is serverless; a AWS manage the entire execution infrastructure. C) Incorrect: the charge is by number of requests and execution time (GB-(d) Correct: CPU (and network) scale along with configured memory — increasing memory is the way to give more CPU (e) Incorrect: Lambda can be connected to a VPC to access private resources, such as RDS.
